analysis.summary: The enrichRoutes function in BffApi.ts ignores the functionName property explicitly set in route definitions, causing Lambda functions to be deployed with auto-generated names instead of the intended names. This breaks the explicit naming convention intended by the developer.

bugs.title: enrichRoutes ignores explicit functionName causing wrong Lambda names
bugs.description: The enrichRoutes function destructures only handler, timeout, and memorySize from the route function config, ignoring the functionName property that is now explicitly provided in all route definitions. It then generates a different functionName using a template string, effectively discarding the intended names like 'product-catalogue-qa-app-model' and replacing them with generated names like 'BFF-QA-GET-app-model-stage'.
bugs.risk: Lambda functions will be deployed with unexpected names that don't match the explicit naming convention defined in the routes object. This can break monitoring, logging, IAM policies, or cross-stack references that depend on the specific functionName pattern defined in the code.

notBugs.reason: The CloudFront Function removal is intentional and coordinated with the BffApi route changes. The BFF routes now include the full path prefix (baseUrl), so URL rewriting is no longer needed. The webpack output paths have also been updated to match the new S3 key structure.

The timeout configuration is preserved from the original code. Routes that previously lacked timeout (like price-details, cart-model) continue to use the Lambda default (3s). This is not a new bug introduced by the PR.

Site.ts uses app.name while BffApi.ts uses featureAppName from AppConfig. This could cause a mismatch if they differ, but without evidence that app.name and featureAppName are different values or that this causes runtime errors, this remains speculative.
